title: Investigate per-key shadow-window overlap causing brief unmetered bursts
creator: Maya Patel
description: Summary: We are seeing short-duration bursts of unmetered usage for some orgs and API keys when the rate-engine transitions shards/epochs. Symptoms: transient spikes in allowed requests (seconds-long) that are not reflected in metering aggregates; observed at scale during planned shard reconciliation and some unplanned rebalances. Impact: customers observe token usage that does not increment billing records resulting in revenue undercount (est. $2k-10k/week depending on failover frequency) and product throttles not applied, which can cause noisy neighbor latency spikes and potential SLO violations.
reproduction_steps:
1) Use a load generator to drive steady single-key traffic at near-burst threshold (client: ~120 RPS, per-key burst=100 tokens/sec).
2) Trigger a shard rebalance by toggling shard assignment on staging (k8s label rotate or leader eviction).
3) Observe that for ~1-8s after handoff, throttle decisions allow >2x expected throughput and meter events are missing from the aggregator.
4) Trace shows policy evals on the new primary returning 'allow' due to gap in shadow-window stitching.
Observed artifacts: missing meter RPCs in shard-aggregator logs, KV cache TTL mismatches for per-key epoch tokens, trace IDs: trace=trace-20260307-9a3f, trace=trace-20260308-4b21.
initial_findings:
- Fastpath: policy pre-evaluation cached per-key windows are not being atomically advanced during shard lease transfer.
- Race: lease expiry handler applies a local 'grab' and recomputes window buckets; concurrent inflight requests use old window boundaries before aggregator has received the final debit events.
- Metering: aggregator dedupe logic drops debits that appear out-of-order when they arrive with an older epoch timestamp, causing net delta < actual.
- Partial mitigation observed when we increase write-through debounce (makes window stitching slower but reduces unmetered allowance).
hypothesis: When a shard loses leadership, outstanding requests that were token-charged locally but whose debit message to the aggregator is delayed can be replayed/accepted on the new leader due to overlapping shadow windows. The aggregator's out-of-order handling currently discards debits with timestamp <= last-committed-epoch, which lets a small amount of usage escape billing and enforcement.
logs_and_traces:
Relevant logs stored in GCS: gs://redwood-logs/rate-engine/2026-03/rebalance/*.log. Example trace snippets: - trace-20260307-9a3f: shows request T1 allowed by new leader at t=164s; aggregator receives debit at t=170s but drops due to epoch <= committed_epoch. - pod: rate-engine-rl-7f5d (zone us-west2-a) shows lease-handoff logs 'lease: revoke -> grab' at 2026-03-07T14:03:12Z.
Attached dashboards: runtime->rate_engine->per_key_allow_overrun, billing->aggregator->late_debits (alerts firing).
metrics_impacted:
- per_key_allow_overrun: spike to +150% for affected keys
- aggregator_late_debits: 0.8% of total debits during incidents
- billing_diff_backfill: increasing backlog of unaccounted tokens
- SLO: p99 latency ripple for other tenants during unthrottled period
short_term_mitigation:
1) Enable a temporary conservative enforcement mode that reduces per-key burst window by 50% on new leaders for 30s post-lease. This is a config flip (feature-flag: conservative-post-handoff) that has been tested in staging.
2) Add metric-based alert: aggregator_late_debits > 0.5% for 5m -> pages on-call.
3) Backfill: run aggregator replay job to reconcile debits for windows with missing records (one-off job: billing/reconcile_v2).
long_term_plan:
1) Fix aggregator dedupe semantics: accept debits with older epoch if they carry a monotonic sequence number and apply them idempotently instead of dropping.
2) Implement atomic window advance during lease transfer: leader should publish a 'handoff marker' event with final pending-debits so new leader can reconcile before starting permissive windows.
3) Add end-to-end integration tests simulating shard handoffs with high concurrency, including timing fuzzing.
4) Add telemetry: per-key handoff_latency histogram, and end-to-end debit delivery latency SLA (target < 200ms).
5) Postmortem and billing correction policy: design an automatic backfill + charge notice flow for impacted customers.
work_items: write unit tests for aggregator dedupe logic
current_blockers:
- Need consensus on sequence-number propagation format with storage team (affects wire compatibility).
- Perf concern: handoff marker introduces extra RPCs which must be benchmarked before runtime-1.21 GA.
- Billing team wants proof we can reconcile charges before auto-charging customers.
proposed_schedule: Week 1: implement conservative flag + alerting + run backfill job in staging. Week 2: submit aggregator dedupe fix PR and handoff-marker prototype (code review). Week 3: integration tests + perf benchmarks. Week 4: canary rollout to 10% traffic, monitor metrics, then full rollout.
risks_and_tradeoffs:
- Conservative-post-handoff reduces burst capacity and may increase legitimate throttles (customer experience hit).
- Accepting out-of-order debits increases complexity in aggregator state machine and might require compacting historical seq numbers to bound memory.
- Handoff marker increases cross-node coordination latency for leader elections; need microbenchmarks to ensure it doesn't impact failover times beyond acceptable window.
notes_for_release_notes: Fixes a transient accounting gap during shard leadership changes that could under-report token usage for some customers and briefly bypass throttles. Customers may see corrected billing adjustments after reconciliation.
runbook: Playbook for on-call: 1) Toggle conservative-post-handoff flag. 2) Kick billing reconciliation job with job-id. 3) Monitor p99 latency and aggregator_late_debits for 30m. 4) If mitigation fails, roll back shard migration and open emergency incident.
